articleTitle: Selected Health and Law Issues Regarding Mobile Communications with Respect to 5G
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: Over the next years the demand of wireless communication will increase tremendously. More and more mobile end devices require a high data rate connection e.g. to a smart home (Internet of Things, IoT) or to the internet. The radiation power pattern of base stations and mobile end devices will completely change for the 5G Next Generation Mobile Network technology which will use frequency bands up to 100 GHz. Therefore the electromagnetic exposure especially to human body will increase in the future, because most of the wireless connections are realized in RF technology. In this contribution two different measurement setups are presented. The first shows the electromagnetic radiation regarding a base station powered by a mobile phone provider over a timespan of a number of days. The second figures out the electromagnetic radiation of a handheld mobile end device to a human head in an area with very poor reception values. The results of those measurements where compared with legal and health limits. All measured and calculated results regarding the base stations were within the legal exposure limits. The calculated legal exposure limits of mobile devices were exceeded twice in areas within very poor reception values. Regarding the expected higher bandwidth and corresponding higher electromagnetic exposure to human bodies in future there have to be periodic measurements to comply with radiation limits.

articleTitle: A Study on Location Information Screening Method for Ship Application Using AIS Recorded Data
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: We focus on the relationship between real-time data in the automatic information system (AIS) station on each ship and between each ship. However, these types of stored recorded data can become big amounts of data. If these data are stored using traditional methods, the data analysis would take too much time. In this study, we focus on the recorded and stored AIS data in the own ship AIS station. The purpose of this study is to present a method to preprocess big data for screening. In particular, Class A AIS stations report their location information (Message ID 1/2/3) autonomously every 2-10 seconds, depending on the ship's speed and/or course changes. We concluded that position data (Message IDs), including the characteristics of the track, are obtained when the ship is steered for changing course. In this paper, we propose a method to use Message ID as the location data, including the characteristics of the track when maneuvering for course change. First, we propose a method to automatically extract the location data of other ships and ships that the ship's AIS station acquired during the voyage. In addition, we investigated these data Message IDs separately and performed a comparison. According to the evaluation results, the extracted data required less storage space and retained many characteristics of the track. It was possible to show that this screening method can be applied using fewer operational processes and without increasing time and cost.

articleTitle: Simulation Studies of Communication Systems with Mutual Overflows and Threshold Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: In the article, the research results on the effectiveness of overflow technique in multi-service networks have been presented. Two kinds of overflows have been considered: overflow between primary resources (the same level of hierarchy), i.e., mutual overflow; and traffic overflow between primary and secondary resources, i.e., hierarchical overflow. In the first place, a traffic offered to the specific primary resources, when they are busy, is forwarded to neighboring primary resources. In the case, when the request cannot be handled by any of primary resources, it is overflowed to secondary resources. Additionally, in the research threshold compression mechanism was considered, according to which - for certain levels of resource occupancy - a reduced amount of resources is allocated for new requests in respect to the requested amount. The effectiveness of the overflow and compression mechanisms has been evaluated using the blocking probability, number of the served requests and amount of the carried traffic. The outcome of the work can be used in planning and dimensioning of multi -service systems with separated resources, e.g. in data centres.

articleTitle: Motor Vessel LAN - Design, Implementation, and Operation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: Resulting from the spread of computer usage, substantial advances in the development of network technologies, and the increasingly common ability to connect to the Internet, today's world is undergoing a significant evolvement in the methods of communication. Aboard motor vessels, the widespread dependence on computer technology by various forms of equipment has created a need to be organically connected via onboard LAN in order to exchange information. This paper, then, proposes a practical Shipboard LAN System configuration based on the practical application of information obtained from usage aboard the Training Ship (TS) FUKAE MARU - the Kobe University training / research ship. Though fitted with a basic Shipboard LAN System that was up to date when the vessel was constructed approximately three decades ago, over time, as network demands have increased, improvements - such as a duplicate system for backup and the installation of Wi-Fi Access Points enabling connection at anywhere inboard ship this vessel - were made. As a result, the efficient utilization of the Shipboard LAN, all data - gathered in a server PC - is able to be delivered via the LAN and thereby realize an advanced navigation system. In addition to a description of the process and its results, a proposal for the practical usage of the Shipboard LAN System applications is presented.

articleTitle: Evaluations of Low-Cost Decoding Methods for 1090 MHz SSR Signals
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: l,090 MHz secondary surveillance radar (SSR) signals received at airports from Mode A/C and S transponders suffer mostly from garbling, fading and multipath. Due to these radio wave propagation effects, the received overlapped signals result in pulse distortion and inter-symbol interferences (lSI) and eventually they cause bit errors. To cope with these issues, decoding methods based on threshold and edge detection principles are evaluated in this work. Herein we have shown new evaluations of decoding methods in the time domain with the corresponding signal filtering and validated with real-world data from the Salzburg airport in Austria. Each of the installed receiving stations uses a dipole antenna with a single receiving stream. Especially, the multilevel threshold detection decoding technique, which exploits multilevel thresholding for peak detection, leads to a significant lower bit error rate (BER) compared to the common known decoding method of Mode S secondary radars. Furthermore, occurring bit errors are marked and all methods are low-cost implementable on a field programmable gate array (FPGA) and digital signal processor.

articleTitle: Influence of On-Off Keying Duty Cycle on BER in Wireless Optical Communication Up to 75 Mbit/s Using an SPAD and a RC LED
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: In this paper we analyze the influence of the on-off keying duty cycle on the achievable bit error ratio (BER) in a optical wireless communication (OWC) system which employs a single photon avalanche diode (SPAD) based receiver and a red LED transmitter as a source. In a line of sight (LOS) channel configuration at a transmitting distance of 3 m the bit error rate (BER) improvement is demonstrated by varying the duty cycle of return to zero (RZ) line coding at 50 Mbit/s. Compared to NRZ line coding at the same transmitting distance and data rate the BER improvement is almost up to an order of magnitude lower when RZ coding is used. The reached BER values are below the limit for forward error correction (FEC) thus promising the increase of the maximum achievable transmission distance. Additionally, the BER improvement allowed the transmission below FEC limit over 3 m at an increased data rate of 75 Mbit/s.

articleTitle: Low Complexity Multi-User Detection in the Forward Link of High Throughput Satellite Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: Multi-user detection (MUD) is an advanced interference mitigation technique relevant for high throughput satellites in the forward link to mitigate co-channel interferences introduced by an aggressive frequency reuse. MUD mitigates the interference directly at the receiver on ground and requires therefore a higher complexity in the user terminals. In this work a software-based system demonstrator was utilized to analyze performance-efficient implementations of MUD in the receiving unit on ground. The number of detector and, in further consequence, decoder iterations were identified as crucial factors in this context. The study compares the performance in terms of processing speed, accuracy and required iterations.

articleTitle: A Compact Ultra-Wideband Load-Pull Measurement System
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: This paper presents an oscilloscope based load pull measurement system for an ultra-wideband ranging chip. Such a system is intended to characterize a chips radio frequency circuits' behavior under different operating conditions. The gathered measurement results should then be used for the optimization of the chips external circuitry, to reduce power consumption and improve pulse shaping. In this way we want to accomplish longer battery lifetime and higher ranging accuracy. By postprocessing the measurement results the de-embedding of the measurement circuitry is accomplished. Using verification measurements, we validate the performance of the measurement setup and the implemented postprocessing approach.

articleTitle: Textile Integrated Waveguide Switch
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: A switch embedded into a textile integrated waveguide (TIW) was designed for the ISM band 5.8 GHz. Using a 3D knitted fabrics as a substrate, a self-adhesive copper foil for manufacturing conductive surfaces and a conductive thread for the fabrication of side walls, a TIW T -junction was created. PIN diodes in the output branches of the T -junction were used then to switch the transmission between the input port and output ports on or off. PIN diodes controlled conductive posts connecting the top surface and the bottom one of TIW; posts were surrounded by a circular slot. Functionality of the concept of the described textile-integrated switch was proven by simulations and measurements.

articleTitle: Joint Synchronization of Carrier Frequency, Symbol Timing and Sampling Rate in Digital Satellite Receivers
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: Parameter estimation and synchronization is of paramount importance in digital satellite receivers to achieve the challenging objectives in terms of throughput and availability required for next-generation networks. Non-data-aided and car-rier-blind algorithms are most appreciated in this respect, which is frequently realized by a feedback (FB) scheme. In some previous work, it could be shown that both carrier frequency and symbol timing might be recovered successfully with this approach, avoiding this way the distortion of waveforms at the output of the receiver matched filter (MF). On top of that, it could be verified that the jitter variances exhibit no error floor, mainly achieved via a second filter with particular properties operated in parallel to the receiver MF. In the current paper, this FB structure is extended insofar as timing or sampling drifts can be synchronized as well, which is primarily reached by an appropriate design of the loop filter needed for timing recovery. Finally, successful tracking and acquisition is exemplified by numerical results.

articleTitle: Free-Space Optical Communications - Standardisation Issues
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: In the meantime, Optical Wireless is a well-established Communication Technology. In this talk, Free Space Optics (FSO) is considered within the focus of regulations and standardisation-bodies for future applications. The FSO-Technology is compared to other Communication Technologies (including wireless technologies, like WLAN and satellite communications) regarding those aspects. ITU, IEC, and IEEE International standards for Free-Space Optical links will be reviewed. Emphasis will be put to co-existence and compatibility of neighbouring systems, propagation atmospheric conditions, visible light communications, and laser safety issues.

articleTitle: Single-Mode Light Generation in DFB Fiber Laser: Wavelength-Scale Electromagnetic Modelling by the Method of Single Expression
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: Distributed feedback (DFB) semiconductor and fiber lasers are widely used in different areas of science, technology, medicine, etc. Till now stable single-mode radiating fiber lasers operating in ultraviolet, visible and infrared bands are under strong demand. Single-mode operation of fiber lasers is very advantageous for telecommunication, spectroscopy, sensors applications, etc. However, there is a lack of a wavelength-scale electromagnetic analysis of such fiber lasers at the single-mode radiation. In the current work the results of correct wavelength-scale electromagnetic analysis of radiation of DFB fiber lasers are presented. For wavelength-scale analysis the non-traditional method of single expression is used. In accordance with the known information, single-mode radiation from DFB fiber laser is observed at the pi-shift in the middle of permittivity sinusoidal modulation of an amplifying fiber. Numerically obtained wavelength-scale distributions of electric field component and power flow density within the DFB amplifying fiber will be useful in designing single-mode radiating DFB fiber lasers.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of a Spread-Spectrum Satellite Return Link Protocol for Small Antenna Sizes
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: A system study on the performance of nonorthogonal spread-spectrum Aloha waveforms applied on the return link for narrowband fixed GEO satellite services such as M2M/IoT in Ku-band is presented. In this context the performance of small antennas is evaluated based on a model extrapolating the link performance of the strongest received terminal to the performance of the entire system. Link budget calculations including applicable regulatory limits are employed to evaluate the system performance. Useful optimizations are demonstrated improving the latter remarkably. Furthermore, system sizing aspects are discussed with particular attention to the satellite transponder sensitivity.

articleTitle: Upgrade of an Astronomical Telescope for Satellite Laser Ranging Up to Geostationary Targets
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: Satellite Laser Ranging (SLR) is a well-established, mature technique for precise orbit determination (POD). Its overall performance however significantly relies not only on the specific hard- and software equipment of the respective SLR stations - which is relatively expensive -, but also on their global distribution. Upgrading already existing astronomical telescopes with a low-energy laser (e.g, 15 μJ / 2 kHz / 532 nm), plus single-photon detector plus a suitable event timer - all relatively low cost units - creates new SLR systems, which allows laser ranging from Low Earth Orbits (LEO) up to Geosynchronous Orbit (GSO) targets.

articleTitle: A Look into the Future of Sports: A Study of the Actual State of the Art - the Microsoft HoloLens and Augmented Reality
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: This paper addresses the possibilities of implementation of an augmented reality solution for sports domain, using the Microsoft HoloLens device. The authors investigate the possibilities of the platform in its current state and present a prototype solution for visual presentation of match related statistics and other data, provided by the Sportradar company. The architecture and results of the solution are presented as well as its benefits and drawbacks.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Mobile Radio Links as Command-and-Control Links for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: The Joint Authorities for Rulemaking on Unmanned Systems (JARUS) publishes recommendations and guidelines for Unmanned Aerial Systems (UASs). UASs consist of an unmanned aircraft, a ground control station (GCS) and a secure command-and-control (C2) link as a bidirectional connection of these systems. To operate an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), a secure C2 link within and beyond the visual line of sight (VLOS and BVLOS) is inevitable. For such connections, many different wireless technologies are possible. In terms of availability and infrastructure, the mobile radio network seems to be a promising technology. In this article, third- (3G) and fourth-generation (4G) mobile radio modems were evaluated to determine if they are suitable as C2 hardware. In order to use them as a primary link, different test scenarios on the ground and in the air were set up and tested. The results are summarized as recommendations for upcoming regulations for UA Vs.

articleTitle: A Fair Computational Resource Management Strategy in C-RAN
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: A resource management strategy is presented, aiming at managing the computational resources of a Base Band Unit pool (BBU-pool), in Cloud Radio Access Network. The goal is the efficient use of computational resources, while striking an optimum balance amongst all the BBUs in high demand conditions that lead to computational resource leakage. To this end, the BBUs required computational resources are estimated on the basis of a time frame, based on user processing and type of running services. A game theory approach of bargaining is employed in order to achieve the optimal allocation policy for the BBU-pool computational resource management. An individual BBU is assigned with a bargaining power based on the number of its user processing and on the services priority level. The Generalized Nash Bargaining Solution is then applied as a strategy to distribute computational resources in a fair manner. In order to evaluate model efficiency, a simple scenario is considered. Simulation results confirm that the model allocates computational resources according to the BBUs bargaining power. Moreover, numerical results show that 100% of the available computational capacity is used in case of need.

articleTitle: Measurement of IPTV Qualitative Parameters on EPON/VDSL2 Topology
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: Ahstract- The future of telecommunication networks lies in the area of multimedia services that are offered to end customers. The article discusses the possibilities of deploying IPTV service for a hybrid type of telecommunication topology, which is formed by EPON/VDSL2 systems. The advantage of such topologies is the use of already existing telecommunication network and verification of qualitative features of the distributed IPTV data flows at the same moment. Therefore, the main outputs of this article are the possibilities of distributing data packets by means of multicast or unicast operations. The basic qualitative parameters of the video and data flows (PSNR, MSE, and SSIM) were evaluated with the help of the software tool - MSU Video Quality Measurement Tool.

articleTitle: SOLEIL: Streaming of Large-Scale Events Over Internet Clouds
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: This paper deals with the design and realization of a streaming platform specifically targeted at large-scale and live, low-delay, events. The streaming platform, called SOLEIL, is conceived to be compliant, at its edge nodes, with the WebRTC specification, meaning users can take advantage of its capabilities using a simple browser. Details on both the design and implementation processes are provided, together with some pointers on how to dynamically deploy the main SOLEIL components in the cloud.

articleTitle: Next Generation Robotics Swarm Positioning and Collision Detection Under a Case of Disaster
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: The positioning and control of objects in indoor environments are still an open and very challenging problem, especially in a case of disasters. Due to this, the authors presented a composite algorithm for estimation of the position and collision of the robots in a swarm in indoor environment under a case of a fire disaster. The proposed algorithm is based on a combination of Time Difference of Arrival, Radio Signal Strength Indicator fingerprint and distance evaluation using ultrasound technology. The investigations, scenarios of robots' navigation in a testbed, results of robots' position as well errors in position evaluation are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: On the L0-Norm Based Sparse Time-Frequency Distribution Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: Joint time-frequency (TF) domain often provides an additional insight into the observed phenomenon, rather than observing the phenomenon in the time and frequency domain separately. Recently, a compressive sensing (CS) approach has been proposed to solve one of the main problems of the signal TF representation: the removal of artefacts. These artefacts, also called the cross-terms, are a mathematical byproduct of the time-frequency distribution (TFD) calculation, and are usually suppressed with a low-pass filtering, the procedure which also reduces the TF resolution. The resolution loss, in the CS-based approach, is avoided by an optimization procedure, which enforces the sparsity constraints to the resulting sparse TFD. In this paper, we investigate the application of the l0 -norm based reconstruction algorithms for the sparse TFD calculation. Furthermore, we employ the adaptive CS scheme in order to improve the quality of the resulting sparse TFDs, while reducing the reconstruction algorithm execution time.

articleTitle: Optical Network Softwarization: Technologies, Trends and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: Nowadays, a high level of digitalization, transformation of the industry, machine-to-machine communication, and many other innovative commercial, industrial and private applications set very high requirements on the underlying optical network infrastructure. Mainly for this reason, optical networks are currently undergoing a radical change from traditional static architectures to more dynamic, flexible, and adaptable concepts. In order to optimally support the emerging applications, future optical networks should be able to provide rapid and on-demand provisioning of high data rates in a flexible and efficient manner. In this talk, we will discuss current trends and challenges in the areas of softwarization and virtualization of optical network infrastructure and review various emerging technologies and architectures for future high capacity, efficient, and flexible optical transport networks.

articleTitle: Technologies, Trends and Challenges in Multimedia Content Consumption
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: In recent years we have experienced significant changes in the way people consume multimedia content, specifically audio and video. The high penetration of broadband connectivity has provided a basis for on demand content consumption, which is noticeably replacing watching of linear TV and a steady shift from broadcast to broadband content distribution. Additionally, new content formats and devices are becoming ever more popular, providing users with larger video formats such as 4K and 8K. The advent of virtual and augmented reality solutions requires not only a higher bandwidth for content distribution, but also new content interaction modalities and presentation aspects. In this talk, we will discuss the trends, challenges and opportunities in the multimedia content domain and review the aspects of new content formats from the technological and user experience perspective.

publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: Internet; satellite communication; wireless LAN; ships; marine engineering; augmented reality; optical communication; error statistics; multimedia communication; transponders.
